Ivy (PM): Quick triage: Beacon + Nova want a firm launch date but engineering says we need to pick a cutline that balances SLA, security (BYOK), and cost. Need alignment on what goes GA vs. staged. Short answers please.

Ravi (Eng - Runtime): Short: we can deliver private deploy + basic SLA (99.5) without BYOK if we use short-term HSM-proxy shim and ReservedBurst pools. Full BYOK/HSM integration is 3w. Risk: p99 spikes during cold-starts unless we implement prefix cache and a warmup runbook.

Lena (Infra): ReservedBurst pools meaning: spin up unreserved GPUs and attach "burst" credits for peak traffic; cheaper than reserved 24/7 but requires autoscaler hooks and capacity safety nets. One infra-tkt to wire autoscaler -> billing -> capacity: INF-321. ETA 10 business days. Cost delta: ~35% cheaper first month vs reserved.

Omar (Security): BYOK needs KMS workflow + audit hooks. HSM-proxy is acceptable as a contract stop-gap but legal will ask for timeline to full BYOK. Also need ingress allowlist and ephemeral cert rotation. If we promise BYOK in contract, we must deliver within agreed SLA window.

Priya (Customer Success): Beacon says BYOK is non-negotiable in contract language. Nova is more flexible; they'd accept a 90-day roadmap to BYOK. Beacon is top-customer priority.

Alex (Finance): If we do reserved GPUs in all regions for Beacon, ops costs jump ~x3. If we do ReservedBurst and autoscale, we can cap commit and pass-through overages to customer at lower margin. Need pricing direction from Product.

Ivy (PM): Options on table: A) Ship private + BYOK now (longer dev + cost) B) Ship private + HSM-proxy + SLA now, full BYOK in 6-8w C) Ship private without HSM, require BYOK contract clause later (high legal risk). Recommend B to unblock Beacon sales ASAP while committing to BYOK timeline. Thoughts?

Ravi (Eng - Runtime): B is safest tradeoff. For rollout we can add a canary flag and model-fallback. Canary YAML snippet:
```yaml
rollout:
  canary: 5%
  duration: 24h
  fallback: model-small-v2
  warmup: true
```
Need INF-321 + SEC-204 before canary.

Lena (Infra): OK on B pending INF-321 and a network window. I'll prioritize INF-321 and tag netops.

Omar (Security): I'll sign off on HSM-proxy approach if we get a documented plan and timeline to BYOK, plus proof-of-concept with audit logs. I'll create SEC-204 and attach acceptance criteria.

Alex (Finance): If Product approves pass-through pricing for burst overage, we can proceed with B with minimal impact to margin. Need product to confirm.

Priya (Customer Success): I'll tell Beacon we can do HSM-proxy + firm 8-week BYOK commitment and ask them to accept a 99.5 SLA initially. Will capture in the CRF.

Ivy (PM): Decision: go with B (HSM-proxy + canary + 8-week BYOK commitment). Owners: Ravi(runtime) for warmup + fallback, Lena(infra) for INF-321, Omar(sec) for SEC-204, Alex(finance) for pricing, Priya(customer). Action items: INF-321, SEC-204, pricing note, canary plan. Please post short updates in this thread.

Ravi (Eng - Runtime): Posting first quick update: implemented warmup stub and ran load test: private-canary-1 p99=185ms after warmup, cold-start p99=420ms. Need warmup cron for 30m cadence during ramp.

ci-bot: build serve-scale/hsm-proxy#489 passed :white_check_mark:

Lena (Infra): INF-321 created and assigned to infra-cloud. ETA 9 business days.

Omar (Security): SEC-204 created with BYOK timeline and audit acceptance. Will drop checklist by EOD.

Alex (Finance): Pricing approach: pass-through for burst overage + 10% buffer margin approved. Sending PR to pricing docs.

Ivy (PM): Great, thanks. If nothing blocks, I'll lock launch date Monday morning and feed this status to Sales. If anyone hits a blocker, ping me immediately. :rocket:
